These are starting questions for the field guide. Follow one as far as it remains interesting;
the experiment and the explanation can change together.

## How much control should an agent have? {#agent-control}

Understand the tradeoff between a model choosing its next action and a workflow whose transitions are explicit.

**A small way to investigate:** Give two implementations the same small task, tools and stop condition. Inspect what they do when a tool fails.

**Related areas:** [Agents and workflows](topics/agents-and-workflows.qmd) · [Tools and MCP](topics/tools-and-mcp.qmd) · [OpenAI interfaces and SDKs](topics/openai-interfaces.qmd) · [Evaluation and error analysis](topics/evaluation.qmd)


```{=html}
<ul class="annotated-sources"><li><div><a href="https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Choose an agent runtime</a><small>official guide</small></div><p>Compares Responses, Agents SDK and managed Agents API.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://www.anthropic.com/engineering" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Anthropic Engineering</a><small>blog</small></div><p>Detailed accounts of building, evaluating, and deploying agent systems.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Hugging Face smolagents</a><small>project</small></div><p>A relatively compact agent library useful for reading an execution loop end to end.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">LangGraph</a><small>project</small></div><p>Useful for learning persistent agent workflows and control over state transitions.</p></li></ul>
```

[Follow the investigation](investigations/smolagents-and-langgraph.qmd).

## How do I know the system improved? {#evaluation}

Separate a convincing answer from a useful result. Look at failures, supporting evidence and the behavior of the whole system.

**A small way to investigate:** Keep a few representative inputs and expected behaviors. Compare one change against the same cases and inspect the disagreements.

**Related areas:** [Evaluation and error analysis](topics/evaluation.qmd) · [Retrieval and grounding](topics/retrieval-and-grounding.qmd) · [Production and inference](topics/production-and-inference.qmd)


```{=html}
<ul class="annotated-sources"><li><div><a href="https://hamel.dev/" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Hamel Husain&#x27;s Blog</a><small>blog</small></div><p>Concrete guidance on looking at data, debugging failures, and measuring AI products.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/evaluation-best-practices" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Evaluation best practices</a><small>official guide</small></div><p>Task-specific evaluation principles despite legacy product references.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://github.com/promptfoo/promptfoo" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">promptfoo</a><small>project</small></div><p>A practical way to turn AI behavior into repeatable test cases and compare configurations.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://github.com/Arize-ai/phoenix" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Arize Phoenix</a><small>project</small></div><p>A concrete way to learn what an AI application does through traces and evaluation records.</p></li></ul>
```

## What belongs in the model's context? {#context}

Connect instructions, memory, retrieval and tool results to the information the model actually needs.

**A small way to investigate:** Try one task with different evidence selections. Record what the model could see and which answer that evidence supported.

**Related areas:** [Model behavior and context](topics/models-and-context.qmd) · [Retrieval and grounding](topics/retrieval-and-grounding.qmd) · [Tools and MCP](topics/tools-and-mcp.qmd) · [Security and trust boundaries](topics/security.qmd)


```{=html}
<ul class="annotated-sources"><li><div><a href="https://huggingface.co/learn/context-course/unit0/introduction" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Hugging Face Context Course</a><small>course</small></div><p>Connects the extension mechanisms you already use with the context an agent needs to work well.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/retrieval" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Retrieval</a><small>official guide</small></div><p>Separates vector-store search from answer generation.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://simonwillison.net/" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Simon Willison&#x27;s Weblog</a><small>blog</small></div><p>Hands-on model experiments, annotated releases, practical tools, and prompt-injection coverage.</p></li><li><div><a href="https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/getting-started/intro" class="" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Model Context Protocol introduction</a><small>standard</small></div><p>The protocol’s own explanation of hosts, clients, servers and external capabilities.</p></li></ul>
```

## What makes an experiment useful to someone else? {#deployment}

Follow the path from a working example to a reliable, understandable part of a person's work.

**A small way to investigate:** Ask someone to try a narrow workflow. Watch where they wait, lose trust or need to correct the result.

**Related areas:** [Product and field engineering](topics/product-and-field-engineering.qmd) · [Production and inference](topics/production-and-inference.qmd) · [Security and trust boundaries](topics/security.qmd) · [Multimodal and realtime systems](topics/multimodal.qmd)
